title: Codegen: Fix Numeric Type System
description: The Go code generator emits incorrect numeric types causing compilation failures in 35 of 50 failing example files. Root causes: (1) float64-typed constants/expressions assigned to float32/int16/int32 variables, (2) mixed-type binary operations (float32+float64, int16*float64), (3) runtime functions accept/return float64 but variables may be float32/int16. This epic covers all type-casting fixes needed for the transpiled Go output to compile.

title: Fix type casts in variable declarations and assignments (emitLet)
description:
File: internal/codegen/codegen.go, function emitLet()

PROBLEM: When emitting 'var X float32 = <expr>', if <expr> evaluates to a float64-typed value (e.g. from a runtime call or DATA/READ), Go compilation fails with 'cannot use float64 as float32'.

ROOT CAUSE: emitLet() was partially fixed to add type casts, but still misses cases:
1. Expressions involving runtime function returns (rt.Val, rt.Timer return float64)
2. DATA/READ type-switch pattern assigns float64 tv_ to int16/float32 vars
3. Compound expressions where sub-expressions are float64

FIX NEEDED:
- In emitLet(), always wrap the RHS in a cast to the LHS variable's Go type:
  var X_sng float32 = float32(<expr>)
- For the DATA/READ type-switch pattern (tv_ assignments), cast tv_ to the target type:
  case float64: A_pct = int16(tv_)
  case float64: S_sng = float32(tv_)

AFFECTED FILES (19): doloop.go, hypotenuse.go, random_numbers.go, swap_demo.go, while_wend.go, write_output.go, clear_demo.go, seq_file_read.go, seq_file_write.go, fibonacci.go, data_read.go, exit_flow.go, random_file.go, read_scores.go, write_file.go, on_gosub.go, on_goto.go, if_block.go, select_case.go

TEST: After fix, regenerate examples and verify these files compile with 'go build'.

title: Fix type casts in binary operations (emitExpr InfixExpression)
description:
File: internal/codegen/codegen.go, emitExpr() for *ast.InfixExpression

PROBLEM: Go does not allow binary ops between different numeric types. Generated code like 'float32 + float64' or 'int16 * float64' fails with 'invalid operation: mismatched types'.

ROOT CAUSE: emitExpr() emits 'left op right' without type-checking. When left is float32 var and right is float64 literal/expr, types mismatch.

FIX OPTIONS (pick one):
A) Type inference: track each expression's Go type, cast the narrower operand to the wider type
B) Simple: when the codegen detects a binary op where one side is a typed variable and the other is a literal or different-typed expr, wrap the narrower side in a cast
C) Pragmatic: emit all arithmetic operands as float64, then cast the result back to the target type at assignment

RECOMMENDED: Option B - in emitExpr for InfixExpression, determine the Go type of left/right. If they differ, cast the narrower to the wider. Requires a goTypeForExpr() helper that returns the Go type of an arbitrary expression.

AFFECTED FILES (16): doloop.go, factorial.go, factorial_recursive.go, color_table.go, incr_decr.go, while_wend.go, select_case.go, if_block.go, tempconv.go, timer_bench.go, random_numbers.go, gorilla.go, inkey_loop.go, str_val.go

title: Codegen: Fix INPUT and DATA/READ Emission
description: INPUT statements are emitted using DATA/READ (dataPool/dataIdx) instead of stdin prompts. Files that have DATA statements but no INPUT sometimes lack dataPool/dataIdx declarations. 10 example files affected: input_demo.go, line_input.go, exit_flow.go, if_block.go, on_gosub.go, on_goto.go, select_case.go, tempconv.go, data_read.go, read_scores.go.

title: Emit INPUT statements as fmt.Scan/bufio reads instead of DATA/READ
description:
File: internal/codegen/codegen.go

PROBLEM: BASIC INPUT "Prompt"; A$, B% is emitted using the DATA/READ dataPool pattern:
  A_str = fmt.Sprint(dataPool[dataIdx]); dataIdx++
This reads from a compile-time data array, not stdin. The program hangs or panics if there is no DATA.

ROOT CAUSE: The parser creates ReadStatement nodes for INPUT (or the codegen treats InputStatement the same as ReadStatement). The correct behavior is fundamentally different: INPUT reads from the user at runtime via stdin.

FIX NEEDED:
1. Check how InputStatement is defined in ast.go and how the parser creates it.
2. In emitStatement(), add a case for *ast.InputStatement (or the correct node type).
3. Emit proper stdin reading code:

   BASIC: INPUT "Enter name: "; Name$
   Go:    fmt.Print("Enter name: ")
          scanner := bufio.NewScanner(os.Stdin)
          scanner.Scan()
          Name_str = scanner.Text()

   BASIC: INPUT "Enter X,Y: "; X!, Y!
   Go:    fmt.Print("Enter X,Y: ")
          fmt.Scan(&X_sng, &Y_sng)

   BASIC: LINE INPUT "Full line: "; L$
   Go:    fmt.Print("Full line: ")
          scanner.Scan()
          L_str = scanner.Text()

4. The runtime already has rt.InputPrompt(prompt string) string in io.go which could be used.

5. Add "bufio" and "os" to imports when INPUT is used.

AFFECTED FILES: input_demo.go, line_input.go, tempconv.go, gorilla.go

TEST: Parse input_demo.bas, verify output uses fmt.Scan or rt.InputPrompt, not dataPool.

title: Always emit dataPool/dataIdx when DATA statements exist
description:
File: internal/codegen/codegen.go, emitPreamble() and collectLabelsAndData()

PROBLEM: Some files reference dataPool and dataIdx variables but they are never declared, causing "undefined: dataPool" and "undefined: dataIdx" errors. This happens when:
1. A file has DATA statements but the dataPool declaration is not emitted
2. A file has READ statements referencing DATA but no DATA statements exist
3. INPUT is incorrectly emitted as READ (separate task), causing dataPool references

ROOT CAUSE: collectLabelsAndData() collects DATA values into a pool. The pool is emitted in the preamble only if there are DATA values. But READ statements reference dataPool/dataIdx even when the pool is empty.

FIX NEEDED:
1. In emitPreamble(), always emit dataPool/dataIdx declarations if ANY ReadStatement exists in the AST (not just if DATA values exist):
   var dataPool []interface{}
   _ = dataPool
   dataIdx := 0
   _ = dataIdx

2. Alternatively, only emit these when both DATA and READ are present.

3. Better yet: fix INPUT emission (separate task) so it does not use dataPool, which reduces the number of files needing dataPool.

AFFECTED FILES: exit_flow.go, if_block.go, on_gosub.go, on_goto.go, select_case.go, tempconv.go, input_demo.go, line_input.go

TEST: After fix, verify these files no longer have "undefined: dataPool" errors.

title: Wire up FileManager and emit OPEN/CLOSE statements
description:
File: internal/codegen/codegen.go

PROBLEM: OPEN and CLOSE emit TODO stubs:
  // TODO: declare fm *rt.FileManager if not done
  _ = "DATA.TXT"; _ = rt.FileModeOutput; _ = float64(1); _ = 0 // OPEN
  _ = float64(1) // CLOSE #

ROOT CAUSE: emitOpen() emits placeholder assignments instead of actual FileManager calls. Line 1081 in codegen.go.

FIX NEEDED:
1. Add needFileManager bool to CodeGenerator struct
2. In emitPreamble(), if needFileManager is true, emit:
   fm := rt.NewFileManager()
   defer fm.FileCloseAll()
3. In emitOpen(), emit:
   OPEN "file" FOR OUTPUT AS #1  ->  fm.FileOpen(1, "file", rt.FileModeOutput, 0)
   OPEN "file" FOR INPUT AS #1   ->  fm.FileOpen(1, "file", rt.FileModeInput, 0)
   OPEN "file" FOR APPEND AS #1  ->  fm.FileOpen(1, "file", rt.FileModeAppend, 0)
   OPEN "file" FOR RANDOM AS #1 LEN=128 -> fm.FileOpen(1, "file", rt.FileModeRandom, 128)
   OPEN "file" FOR BINARY AS #1  ->  fm.FileOpen(1, "file", rt.FileModeBinary, 0)
4. In emitClose(), emit:
   CLOSE #1  ->  fm.FileClose(1)
   CLOSE     ->  fm.FileCloseAll()

The runtime FileManager API (fileio.go):
  FileOpen(num int, name string, mode FileMode, recLen int) error
  FileClose(num int) error
  FileCloseAll()

title: Emit PRINT#, INPUT#, WRITE#, FIELD, LSET, PUT#, GET#, SEEK statements
description:
File: internal/codegen/codegen.go, emitStatement() default case (line 479)

PROBLEM: These file I/O statements fall through to the catch-all default in emitStatement() and emit TODO comments:
  // TODO: PRINT#
  // TODO: INPUT#
  // TODO: WRITE#
  // TODO: FIELD
  // TODO: LSET
  // TODO: PUT (file)
  // TODO: GET (file)
  // TODO: SEEK

ROOT CAUSE: No case handlers for these AST node types in emitStatement().

FIX NEEDED - map each BASIC statement to the FileManager API in runtime/fileio.go:

  PRINT #1, expr1; expr2  ->  fm.FilePrint(1, false, val1, val2)
  PRINT #1, expr1, expr2  ->  fm.FilePrint(1, false, val1, val2) // comma-separated
  INPUT #1, var1, var2     ->  vals := fm.FileInput(1, 2); var1 = vals[0]; var2 = vals[1]
  LINE INPUT #1, var$      ->  var_str = fm.FileLineInput(1)
  WRITE #1, expr1, expr2   ->  fm.FileWrite(1, val1, val2)
  FIELD #1, 20 AS A$, 10 AS B$  ->  fm.Field(1, []rt.FieldSpec{{20,"A"},{10,"B"}})
  LSET A$ = expr           ->  fm.Lset(1, "A", expr)
  RSET A$ = expr           ->  fm.Rset(1, "A", expr)
  PUT #1, recnum            ->  fm.RandomPut(1, recnum)
  GET #1, recnum            ->  fm.RandomGet(1, recnum)
  SEEK #1, pos              ->  fm.FileSeekPos(1, pos)

Steps:
1. Check which AST node types exist for these statements (in ast.go)
2. Add emitter functions for each
3. If AST nodes are missing, add them to ast.go and parser first

title: Codegen: Fix Numeric Type System
description:
The Go code generator emits incorrect numeric types causing compilation failures in 35 of 50 failing example files. This is the single biggest source of errors. The root cause is that the codegen emits float64 wrappers around all numeric constants and runtime functions return float64, but BASIC variables may be typed as float32, int16, or int32. This epic covers all type system fixes needed for correct Go output.

Affected error categories:
- float64 constant assigned to float32/int16/int32 variables (19 files)
- float64 value from DATA/READ assigned to non-float64 vars (7 files)
- float64 return values from rt.* functions assigned to float32/int16 (5 files)

title: Fix SUB calls emitted as unused variable assignments
description:
File: internal/codegen/codegen.go, emitStatement() for CallSubStatement / emitFunctionCall default case

PROBLEM: BASIC SUB calls like CALL Greet("World") or just Greet "World" are emitted as:
  Greet := func() { ... }  // SUB definition (declared and not used)
  Greet("World")           // call to undefined local function
or sometimes as:
  result := Greet("World") // void function used as value

This causes two Go errors: "declared and not used" and "void function used as value".

ROOT CAUSE: The codegen emits SUB definitions as Go closures assigned to variables (var Greet = func(){}), but then SUB CALLs are emitted as standalone function calls to the variable name. If the SUB has no callers, the variable is unused. If it does have callers, the call may try to capture a return value from a void function.

FIX NEEDED:
1. Emit SUB definitions as Go functions (not closures):
   func Greet(Name_str string) { ... }
   instead of:
   Greet := func(Name_str string) { ... }

2. Emit SUB calls as bare function calls (no return value capture):
   Greet("World")

3. Handle CALL keyword: CALL Greet("World") -> Greet("World")

4. Handle the no-CALL syntax: Greet "World" -> Greet("World")

5. For FUNCTION (returns a value), emit as Go func with return type:
   func Add(A_sng, B_sng float32) float32 { ... return result }

AFFECTED FILES: sub_procedure.go (Greet, Add), file_io.go (SequentialOutput, SequentialAppend, SequentialInput), gorilla.go (Intro, GetInputs, and many more SUBs), random_file.go, seq_file_write.go, write_file.go

title: Implement ON ERROR GOTO and RESUME codegen
description:
File: internal/codegen/codegen.go

PROBLEM: ON ERROR GOTO label and RESUME/RESUME NEXT are emitted as TODO comments:
  // TODO: ON ERROR GOTO ErrorHandler
  // TODO: RESUME NEXT

These are BASIC error-trapping mechanisms. The runtime already has ErrorState (errors.go) with SetHandler(), TriggerError(), Err(), Erl(), ClearError().

BASIC SEMANTICS:
  ON ERROR GOTO label  -- when a runtime error occurs, jump to label
  RESUME               -- retry the statement that caused the error
  RESUME NEXT          -- continue at the statement after the error
  RESUME label         -- continue at the specified label
  ON ERROR GOTO 0      -- disable error trapping

IMPLEMENTATION CHALLENGE: Go does not have BASIC-style error trapping. Options:

A) Panic/recover approach:
   ON ERROR GOTO handler -> defer func() { if r := recover(); r != nil { goto handler } }()
   Problem: goto from deferred function is not allowed in Go.

B) Error-return approach:
   Wrap potentially failing operations in functions that return errors.
   Check error after each call and goto handler if non-nil.
   RESUME NEXT: use a continue-after-error flag.

C) Stub approach (simplest):
   Emit the error handler label and body.
   Emit ON ERROR GOTO as a comment with the errState setup:
     errState.SetHandler("ErrorHandler")
   Errors logged but program continues.

RECOMMENDED: Option C for now. The error handler label is already emitted (it is a GOTO target). Just wire up errState.

AFFECTED FILES: error_handling.go (ON ERROR GOTO, RESUME NEXT), dynamic_array.go (ON ERROR GOTO), gorilla.go (ON ERROR GOTO x3, RESUME x2)

TEST: Parse error_handling.bas, verify errState.SetHandler call in output.

title: Fix redeclared variable and undefined variable scoping issues
description:
File: internal/codegen/codegen.go

PROBLEM: Several codegen issues related to variable scoping:
1. sub_procedure.go: "result redeclared in this block" -- the same variable is declared twice with var
2. gorilla.go: "undefined: Name1_str, Name2_str, NumGames" -- variables set inside a SUB are not visible in main
3. color_table.go: "undefined: Fore_pct" -- variable from one scope used in another
4. random_file.go: "undefined: Rone_str, Rtwo_str" -- same pattern
5. sub_procedure.go: "undefined: sum" -- variable set inside SUB not visible to caller

ROOT CAUSES:
- Variables inside SUB bodies are emitted as local vars (:= or var) making them invisible outside
- When a variable is both declared in a LET inside a loop/block AND used after, it may be redeclared
- SHARED variables (DIM SHARED) should be emitted at package level, not function level

FIX NEEDED:
1. Track all variables in a scope stack. When emitting var declarations, check if the variable was already declared in the same scope -- if so, use assignment (=) not declaration (:= or var).
2. For SUB/FUNCTION: variables marked SHARED should be emitted at package/file level
3. For variables that need to be visible across SUBs and main: emit as package-level vars
4. Consider: in BASIC, all non-local variables are global. The codegen should emit a var block at the top of main() for all variables used in the program, then only use assignment (=) inside SUBs and blocks.

AFFECTED FILES: sub_procedure.go (redeclared, undefined), color_table.go (undefined), gorilla.go (undefined), random_file.go (undefined)

title: Fix dollar-suffixed builtins emitted as array accesses
description:
Files: internal/parser/parser.go (parseIdentifierExpression) and internal/codegen/codegen.go (emitArrayAccess, emitFunctionCall)

PROBLEM: 14 BASIC builtin functions with $ suffixes are emitted as array accesses instead of runtime calls. Examples:
  CHR$(65)     -> CHR_str[int(65)]          should be -> rt.Chr(int(65))
  LEFT$(A$,5)  -> LEFT_str[int(A_str)]      should be -> rt.Left(A_str, int(5))
  MID$(A$,2,3) -> MID_str[int(A_str)]       should be -> rt.Mid(A_str, int(2), int(3))
  HEX$(255)    -> HEX_str[int(255)]         should be -> rt.Hex(int(255))
  UCASE$(A$)   -> UCASE_str[int(A_str)]     should be -> rt.UCase(A_str)
  STRING$(40,"*") -> STRING_str[int(40)]     should be -> rt.StringRepeat(int(40), byte(42))

ROOT CAUSE: In parseIdentifierExpression(), the $ suffix is stripped before checking isBuiltinFunction(). The check reconstructs the name as upper+typeSuffix, but in some code paths the ArrayAccess node is created before the builtin check runs. Multi-arg functions (LEFT$, MID$, STRING$) get multi-dim array treatment -- only first arg becomes the index, rest dumped in a TODO comment.

FULL LIST OF AFFECTED FUNCTIONS (all have runtime implementations):
  CHR$(n)           -> rt.Chr(int(n))           returns (string, error) - strings.go:92
  LEFT$(s$,n)       -> rt.Left(s, int(n))       returns string - strings.go:13
  RIGHT$(s$,n)      -> rt.Right(s, int(n))      returns string - strings.go:25
  MID$(s$,start,len)-> rt.Mid(s, int(start), int(len)) returns string - strings.go:38
  HEX$(n)           -> rt.Hex(int(n))           returns string - strings.go:181
  OCT$(n)           -> rt.Oct(int(n))           returns string - strings.go:190
  BIN$(n)           -> rt.Bin(int(n))           returns string - strings.go:200
  STR$(n)           -> rt.Str(float64(n))       returns string - strings.go:100
  STRING$(n,char)   -> rt.StringRepeat(int(n), byte(char)) returns string - strings.go:249
  ENVIRON$(name$)   -> rt.EnvironGet(name)      returns string - system.go:45
  UCASE$(s$)        -> rt.UCase(s)              returns string - strings.go:208
  LCASE$(s$)        -> rt.LCase(s)              returns string - strings.go:213
  LTRIM$(s$)        -> rt.LTrim(s)              returns string - strings.go:218
  SPACE$(n)         -> rt.Space(int(n))         returns string - strings.go:239

FIX APPROACH (two options):
A) Fix in parser: ensure isBuiltinFunction check runs BEFORE ArrayAccess node creation for $-suffixed identifiers
B) Fix in codegen: in emitArrayAccess(), check if the base name (before mangling) is a known builtin, and re-route to emitFunctionCall() instead

Option A is cleaner. In parseIdentifierExpression(), after stripping the type suffix, reconstruct fullName = upper + typeSuffix and check isBuiltinFunction(fullName) || isBuiltinFunction(upper) BEFORE entering the ArrayAccess branch.

title: Emit correct code for no-argument builtins (INKEY$, DATE$, TIME$, RND, ERR)
description:
File: internal/codegen/codegen.go, emitIdentifier()

PROBLEM: BASIC builtins used without parentheses (INKEY$, DATE$, TIME$, RND, ERR, ERADR) are parsed as Identifier nodes and emitted as bare variable names (INKEY_str, DATE_str, TIME_str, RND, ERR, ERADR) which are undefined in Go.

ROOT CAUSE: The parser creates Identifier nodes for tokens not followed by "(". The codegen emitIdentifier() just runs mangleName() with no special handling.

FIX NEEDED in emitIdentifier():
Add a switch on the uppercase identifier name BEFORE mangleName:

  func (g *CodeGenerator) emitIdentifier(id *ast.Identifier) string {
      upper := strings.ToUpper(id.Name)
      fullUpper := strings.ToUpper(id.Name + id.TypeSuffix)
      switch fullUpper {
      case "INKEY$":  return "rt.Inkey()"     // needs runtime implementation
      case "DATE$":   return "rt.DateStr()"    // already exists in system.go
      case "TIME$":   return "rt.TimeStr()"    // already exists in system.go
      }
      switch upper {
      case "RND":   g.needRng = true; return "rng.Rnd(1)"  // RNG exists in math.go
      case "ERR":   return "float64(errState.Err())"        // ErrorState exists in errors.go
      case "ERADR": return "float64(0) /* ERADR: no memory addresses in transpiled code */"
      }
      return mangleName(id.Name + id.TypeSuffix)
  }

RUNTIME IMPLEMENTATION NEEDED:
- rt.Inkey() string -- non-blocking keyboard read. Add to runtime/io.go or system.go:
  func Inkey() string { return "" } // stub; real impl needs raw terminal I/O
- ERR requires an errState *ErrorState variable in generated main(). Add to emitPreamble():
  errState := rt.NewErrorState()
